title: Orch-RM: Reward Modeling for Multi-Agent Orchestration
claim: Our method achieves a better accuracy-efficiency trade-off than baselines, with higher accuracy at far lower token cost in both inference and training.
layout: 2 side-by-side scatter plots, left-to-right, dotted arrows annotating gains on right
description: Two side-by-side matplotlib plots, both with accuracy (%) on the y-axis and total tokens used on the x-axis, evaluated on AIME 24&25. The left panel, 'MAS Test-Time Scaling', shows line-and-marker curves for five methods, with the number of parallel samples N labeled at each point. The green Orch-RM triangles sit at the top left, with high accuracy at low token cost. Blue LLM-Judge Full Rollout extends to 100M tokens at lower accuracy. Red, purple and orange baselines sit lower. The right panel, 'Orchestrator Continued-Training', is a scatter of single points per method. The green Orch-RM star-like triangle is at the top at 68.33%. Dotted black arrows annotate '3% more acc' and '~10x less token used' against GRPO, DPO, RFT, LLM-as-a-judge and the original checkpoint. Legends sit in the upper right corners.
caption: \ours for MAS Test-Time Scaling (Left) and Continued Orchestrator Training (Right). Left: By operating directly at the orchestration level of MAS, \ours achieves a stronger accuracy-efficiency trade-off for test-time scaling, reducing token usage while improving performance over baselines. Right: Using \ours as the reward signal for continued MAS orchestrator training yields consistent performance gains with substantially lower token usage.
abstract: Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) built on Large Language Models (LLMs) require effective orchestration to coordinate specialized agents, yet training such orchestrators is hindered by limited supervision and high computational cost. We propose Orchestration Reward Modeling (OrchRM), a self-supervised framework for evaluating orchestration quality without human annotations. OrchRM leverages intermediate artifacts from multi-agent executions to construct win-lose pairs for Bradley-Terry reward model training. Unlike existing MAS test-time scaling and orchestrator training frameworks that rely on costly sub-agent rollouts, OrchRM operates directly at the orchestration level, enabling efficient and high-performing reward-guided orchestrator training and MAS test-time scaling. OrchRM improves training efficiency by up to 10x in token usage while improving MAS test-time scaling performance by up to 8% in accuracy. These gains consistently transfer across multiple domains, including mathematical reasoning, web-based question answering, and multi-hop reasoning, demonstrating orchestration-level reward modeling as a scalable direction for robust multi-agent orchestration. Code will be available at https://github.com/Wang-ML-Lab/OrchRM.
